_about: Single source of truth for the #30DayMapChallenge series. Read by shared/style.py (PNG maps) and mirrored as CSS variables in shared/theme.css (web maps). Change a value here AND in theme.css.

font._note: Bitter for headlines (titles, panel headings); Raleway for body text, labels, legends, controls.
font.headline: Bitter
font._web_min_note: Web pages: no text smaller than web_min_px (legends, tooltips, controls), except the footer credit line at web_footer_px.

scales._diverging_note: Low (good/short) = blue, center = neutral, high (bad/long) = amber -> brown. Place the center on a meaningful value (average, median, target).
scales._sequential_note: One hue, light -> dark, for plain magnitude (counts, density).
scales._categorical_note: Identity only. Assign in this fixed order; never cycle. More than 8 categories -> fold into 'Other'. Web: var(--cat-1) … var(--cat-8) in theme.css (dark values switch automatically). PNG: S.CATEGORICAL.
scales._subway_note: NYC subway trunk-line colors (MTA). Use for subway routes instead of the categorical scale: riders already know them. Keys are trunk groups; 'text' is the letter color on a route bullet.

vintage._note: Aged-paper palette for pages that imitate an old map (Day 6). Use S.apply(palette="vintage") for PNGs; on the web put data-palette="vintage" data-theme="light" on <html>: paper stays paper in dark mode. Mirrored in theme.css.
vintage._eras_note: Ordered, old to new, warm to cool. After the brick, pink, yellow, green and blue of old fire insurance atlases. CVD-checked against the paper color.
